questions.q: What is the role of the transport layer, where TCP and UDP operate?
options: Assigning IP addresses to devices
Translating domain names into IP addresses
Managing the actual conversation between two applications, such as breaking data into segments
Encrypting all network traffic by default
questions.explain: IP only handles addressing and routing; the transport layer manages the application-to-application conversation on top of it.

questions.q: What are the three steps of TCP's connection setup, in order?
options: ACK, SYN, SYN-ACK
SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK
Discover, Offer, Request
Request, Offer, Acknowledge
questions.explain: TCP establishes a connection with SYN from the client, SYN-ACK from the server, and a final ACK from the client before data flows.

questions.q: Why does TCP retransmit a segment that was lost in transit?
options: It doesn't — lost segments are simply skipped
Because TCP tracks acknowledgments and notices when expected data never arrived
Because UDP handles all retransmission for TCP
Retransmission only happens during the handshake
questions.explain: TCP numbers and acknowledges every segment, so it can detect a missing one and retransmit it to guarantee reliable, ordered delivery.

questions.q: Why would a live, frequently updating dashboard feed be built on UDP rather than TCP?
options: UDP guarantees every update arrives in order
UDP has no overhead from handshakes or retransmission, and losing an occasional update doesn't matter when a fresher one arrives seconds later
UDP is required for any traffic that updates more than once per minute
TCP cannot be used for dashboards under any circumstances
questions.explain: UDP skips handshakes and retransmission for speed; for data where an occasional dropped update is harmless, that trade-off favors UDP over TCP's guarantees.

questions.q: Which type of traffic is the best fit for TCP rather than UDP?
options: A live voice call
A one-second warehouse sensor ping
A DNS lookup
A checkout transaction that must not lose or scramble any data
questions.explain: Anything where a dropped or out-of-order packet is unacceptable, like a financial transaction, needs TCP's reliable, ordered delivery.
